works.section: The Great Hymn to the Aton
works.title: Dawn
works.source: Great Hymn to the Aton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: The hymn opens with the sunrise: the Aton dawns on the horizon and fills every land with beauty — 'Though Thou art afar, Thy rays are on earth.'

works.section: The Great Hymn to the Aton
works.title: Night
works.source: Great Hymn to the Aton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: When the sun-disk sets, the world falls into a darkness 'like the dead' — the counter-image that makes the dawn a daily act of creation.

works.section: The Great Hymn to the Aton
works.title: The Breath of Life
works.source: Great Hymn to the Aton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: The Aton as giver of life to all that breathes — the child in the womb, the chick crying in the egg-shell — one of the tenderest passages in ancient literature.

works.section: The Great Hymn to the Aton
works.title: How Manifold Are Thy Works
works.source: Great Hymn to the Aton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: The monotheist core: a single creator god who made all lands and peoples, their tongues and skins divided by his hand — 'O Thou sole God, whose powers no other possesseth.'

works.section: The Great Hymn to the Aton
works.title: Thou Art in My Heart
works.source: Great Hymn to the Aton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: The hymn's close, and the heart of Atenism: the god is known to no one save his son Akhnaton, through whom alone the revelation comes — sealed in the name of the King and his queen, Nefertiti.

works.title: The Founding of the City of the Horizon
works.source: Boundary Stela of Akhetaton — trans. A. Weigall
works.note: Akhnaton proclaims to his nobles that the Aton himself — not any man — led him to found his new capital, Akhetaton, on ground claimed by no other god.
